memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Take from this ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat on the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh. This is the ram for the ordination. From the basket of bread made without yeast, which is before the Lord, take one round loaf, one thick loaf with olive oil mixed in, and one thin loaf. Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and have them wave them before the Lord as a wave offering." - Exodus 29:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The offering placed into the priests' hands includes both meat and bread — the portions of the ram together with loaves from the basket. Then they lift it and wave it before the Lord. Their hands are literally filled with what they are giving to God.

The Hebrew idiom for ordination is "to fill the hands," and this is the moment it happens. Their hands are filled with an offering. Before they could serve God, their hands had to be occupied with something given to Him. Ministry began with giving, not with getting.

That is a helpful corrective. We often approach God asking what we will receive from Him. There is nothing wrong with asking — He invites it. But there is something clarifying about coming with hands already full of what we are offering. David refused to give God something that cost him nothing (2 Sam 24:24). What is in your hands today that you could lift up to God — your time, your work, your resources, your willingness? Fill your hands, and lift them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I mostly come to God asking, or also come offering?
What could I deliberately lift up to God today as an offering?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, fill my hands with something worth offering You. Teach me to come not only asking but giving, lifting up my time, my work, and my whole self to You. Amen.
